fixedBefore: 1.0.0 before any result; 1.1.0 after the first mapping run, before coverage; 1.2.0 after the 1.1.0 coverage results (disclosed, both kept).
member: A position is an index member when it is common/preferred equity held long in shares: N-PORT assetCat EC, payoffProfile Long, units NS, valUSD > 0 (money-market/collateral STIV, derivatives DE, cash excluded). In report schedules (N-30D, N-30B-2, N-Q) every line of the common-stock section with a share count and a value.

validation.NPORT: VALID when (sum of member valUSD) / netAssets is within [0.98, 1.01] (an index fund holds its net assets in index equities; up to 2 % may be equitized cash via futures) AND the member count lies in expectedPositions. Otherwise the date is NOT_VALIDATED and counted, never used.
validation.REPORT: VALID when the parsed member values sum to the reported section total (Total Common Stocks / Total Investments in securities of the fund's schedule) within +-1 %, AND the member count lies in expectedPositions. When the document reports no section total the date is NOT_VALIDATED (TOTAL_NOT_FOUND).
validation.duplicates: One date per fund: the original filing; an amendment replaces it only if the original fails validation and the amendment passes.

nameNormalization: upper case; '&' -> ' AND '; drop '/THE' and '/XX' state suffixes; move share-class tokens (CLASS/CL + A-C) into a class tag; remove punctuation; drop filler tokens anywhere (COM, COMMON, STOCK, SHS, SHARES, ORD, ADR, NVS, THE); drop trailing legal-form tokens and a trailing NEW repeatedly (INC, INCORPORATED, CORP, CORPORATION, CO, COMPANY, LTD, LIMITED, PLC, LLC, LP, NV, SA, AG, SE); collapse spaces.

matching.candidates: Our listings with a weekly series in quant/data/market/discover-series-long whose security-master rows are all EQUITY_COMMON; names from company-names.json (companyName and candidate names), the current SEC company_tickers.json title of their ticker (ticker -> securityId only via core/identity.js#securityIdForTicker, ADR-001) and every historical EDGAR name of their CIK (cik-lookup-data.txt).
matching.priceCheck: raw holding price p = value/shares at holding date d; bracket = raw closes (split-adjusted weekly close x product of provider split factors after that bar, quant/engines/return-series.js#splitFactors, ADR-002) of the ISO week containing d and of the previous ISO week; dev = 0 if p inside [min,max], else relative distance to the nearer bound.

tiers.T1_CUSIP_NAME_EXACT: N-PORT CUSIP key whose normalized name/title equals a candidate name, mapped at date d by the per-date rule.
tiers.T2_NAME_UNIQUE: name key (report schedules) or fuzzy name (token-set Jaccard >= 0.9), mapped at date d by the per-date rule.
tiers.T3_UNCERTAIN: name candidates exist but at date d: more than one within tolerance (T3_AMBIGUOUS), none within tolerance (T3_PRICE_NOT_CONFIRMED), no candidate bar (T3_NO_BAR_AT_DATE), confirmation not repeated at an adjacent date (T3_ISOLATED_CONFIRMATION) or share-class conflict (T3_CLASS_CONFLICT). Not used.
tiers.UNMATCHED: no name candidate among our listings.

matching.use: Only T1 and T2 mappings enter the register's securityId field and the coverage.
matching.perDate: mapped at d to c iff c is the only candidate with dev <= 0.05 at d AND (c has a bar at only one key date OR c has dev <= 0.05 at the previous or next key date where c has a bar).
matching.cusipContinuity: For N-PORT CUSIP keys only: when the 1.1.0 per-date rule maps the key to exactly one listing c at >= 2 dates and to no other listing, every further date where c has a bar and bracket deviation <= 0.25 is mapped to c (T1). The 0.25 guard keeps unreflected splits (ratios 0.5, 2, 3, ...) out. Name keys (report schedules) keep the 1.1.0 rule because names are reused across issuers.

coverage.loader: createResearchLoader(root, {identityEvidence: true, corporateActionEvidence: true, listingLifecycleEvidence: true})
coverage.covered: member mapped (T1/T2) to a securityId that the loader returns without error (QUALIFIED) and whose returned points contain a bar within 7 calendar days of the holding date (inside first..last bar).
coverage.measures: per fund and date: share of members (count) and of member value (weight) covered
coverage.qualifiedSubpopulationThreshold: a fund-date qualifies when coverage >= 95 % of members AND >= 99 % of weight; a period qualifies when every validated date in it qualifies

exits: A member key (securityId when mapped T1/T2, else CUSIP, else normalized name) present at date t and absent at every later validated date of the same fund. Fate from SEC submissions of the issuer CIK (Form 25/25-NSE, 15-12B/15-12G/15-15D, 8-K item 2.01) within 400 days after the last holding date; STILL_REPORTING when 10-K/10-Q filings continue more than 400 days later.
quarterPrices: For members without covered series: p = value / shares per date (raw, unadjusted, as reported). Plausibility measured on members with both: |r - 1| distribution per date, exact-week-end dates reported separately.
supersedes: rules-1.1.0.json (its outputs stay in the repository: register/coverage/quarter-prices/price-plausibility-1.1.0)

changesFrom1_0_0.reason: Changed after inspecting the first mapping run (rules 1.0.0) - before any coverage, exit or price number was computed. Validation rules and thresholds are unchanged; all 335 fund-dates validated under 1.0.0 already.
changesFrom1_0_0.nameNormalization: NEW is dropped only as last token (1.0.0 dropped it everywhere and turned BANK OF NEW YORK MELLON into BANK OF YORK MELLON); THE is dropped anywhere (iShares writes PROCTER & GAMBLE CO. (THE)); NVS (non-voting shares) is a filler token.
changesFrom1_0_0.reportParser: column-header rows (Common Stocks / Shares / Value / Security) and date-only lines of continued pages no longer prefix the next security name (observed: COMMON STOCKS SHARES VALUE WELLS FARGO). Exact duplicate rows (same name, shares, value; page repeats in SPY 2019-09-30) are kept once. Member sums and validation results are unchanged by the header fix.
changesFrom1_0_0.candidates: only listings whose security-master rows are all instrument_type EQUITY_COMMON (1.0.0 also admitted preferred listings such as BAC-P-B that carry the issuer name).
changesFrom1_0_0.priceCheck: bracket deviation per holding date instead of one weekly close: the holding date lies inside a week, so p is compared with [min,max] of the previous weekly close and the close of its own ISO week (both as raw prices via split factors); dev = 0 inside, else distance to the nearer bound. 1.0.0 used the week close only; volatile stocks with quarter ends inside the week failed (e.g. LRCX).
changesFrom1_0_0.perDateResolution: mapping is decided per holding date, not per key: a key is mapped at date d to candidate c when c is the only name candidate with dev <= 0.05 at d and c is also within 0.05 at an adjacent key date where it has a bar (or has a bar at only this key date). 1.0.0 used one median over all dates, which merged different issuers sharing a name across eras (ALCOA: Alcoa Inc./Howmet vs Alcoa Corp.).

changesFrom1_1_0.disclosure: Changed AFTER seeing the 1.1.0 coverage results. Both result sets are kept; the README reports the delta.
changesFrom1_1_0.observation: At SPY 2026-06-30 (a Tuesday) large members (Tesla, AMD, Intel, Caterpillar, ...) fell outside the weekly bracket by 5-7 % because the market moved strongly inside the holding week; their N-PORT CUSIP had been mapped to the same listing at the neighbouring dates. Weekly closes cannot bracket intra-week moves.
changesFrom1_1_0.cusipContinuity: For N-PORT CUSIP keys only: when the 1.1.0 per-date rule maps the key to exactly one listing c at >= 2 dates and to no other listing, every further date where c has a bar and bracket deviation <= 0.25 is mapped to c (T1). The 0.25 guard keeps unreflected splits (ratios 0.5, 2, 3, ...) out. Name keys (report schedules) keep the 1.1.0 rule because names are reused across issuers.
changesFrom1_1_0.duplicateKeysInSnapshot: Found by the Python cross-check (part E): two lines with the same name in one snapshot (IWM 2016-12-31 Ferroglobe PLC and a Ferroglobe trust line worth USD 13) shared one key and therefore one mapping. Repeated keys inside one snapshot now get #2, #3, ... in document order and are price-checked separately. Applied to the regenerated 1.1.0 outputs as well (it is a keying fix, not a matching rule).
